name: Liver
description: Largest solid organ, occupying the right upper quadrant. Divided into eight Couinaud segments based on portal and hepatic vein anatomy. Dual blood supply: hepatic artery (25%) and portal vein (75%). On CT: assess for focal lesions, diffuse disease (steatosis, cirrhosis), vascular patency, and biliary dilatation.

name: Spleen
description: Largest lymphoid organ, located in the left upper quadrant posterolateral to the stomach. Lies between the 9th and 11th ribs. On CT: assess for splenomegaly (>13 cm craniocaudal), focal lesions, splenic infarcts, lacerations (trauma), and accessory spleens.

name: Right Kidney
description: Retroperitoneal organ at T12–L3, slightly lower than the left due to the liver. On CT: assess cortical thickness, corticomedullary differentiation, collecting system dilatation (hydronephrosis), stones, masses, and renal vascular anatomy. Contrast phases: corticomedullary (30s), nephrographic (80s), excretory (3–5 min).

name: Left Kidney
description: Retroperitoneal organ at T12–L3, slightly higher than the right. Same imaging assessment as right kidney. The left renal vein courses between the aorta and SMA (nutcracker position). On CT: assess same features as right kidney plus left renal vein compression.

name: Pancreas
description: Retroperitoneal gland extending from the duodenal C-loop (head) to the splenic hilum (tail). Parts: head, uncinate process, neck, body, tail. The main pancreatic duct (Wirsung) joins the common bile duct at the ampulla of Vater. On CT: assess for masses, duct dilatation (>3 mm), calcifications, peripancreatic fat stranding, and atrophy.

name: Stomach
description: J-shaped hollow organ in the left upper quadrant between the esophagus and duodenum. Parts: cardia, fundus, body, antrum, pylorus. On CT: assess wall thickness (<5 mm when distended), masses, ulceration, gastric varices, and gastric outlet obstruction.

name: Gallbladder
description: Pear-shaped sac on the undersurface of the liver (gallbladder fossa). Stores and concentrates bile. Parts: fundus, body, infundibulum (Hartmann pouch), neck. On CT: assess for stones (often hyperdense), wall thickening (>3 mm), pericholecystic fluid, masses, and porcelain gallbladder.

name: Abdominal Aorta
description: Continuation of the descending thoracic aorta below the aortic hiatus (T12). Major branches: celiac trunk, SMA, renal arteries, IMA. Bifurcates into common iliac arteries at L4. On CT: assess diameter (aneurysm >3 cm), mural thrombus, calcification, dissection, and branch vessel patency.

name: Portal Vein
description: Formed by confluence of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins posterior to the pancreatic neck. Carries nutrient-rich blood from the GI tract to the liver. On CT: assess for thrombosis, cavernous transformation, tumor invasion (pancreatic/HCC), and portal hypertension signs (varices, splenomegaly, ascites).

name: Psoas Muscle
description: Paired retroperitoneal muscles originating from T12–L5 vertebral bodies, merging with iliacus to form the iliopsoas, inserting on the lesser trochanter. On CT: assess for asymmetric enlargement (abscess, hematoma), psoas sign (adjacent pathology), and atrophy (sarcopenia marker).
